title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a punctured conformal surface of type (g,ν) with punctures a_i, i ∈ I, card I = ν. Grothendieck works mainly in the hyperbolic oriented case. The previous page argued heuristically that, for fixed X, the 'admissible' families (D_i) of conformal disks around the a_i form a space homeomorphic to R^d with d = card I. These are disks of the kind produced by his conformal surgery, gluing standard caps onto boundary circles of lengths l_i.

σ is the map sending a disk to a standard disk in the tangent line. A conformal disk D_i around a_i has a uniformization (D_i, a_i) ≅ (unit disk, 0), unique up to rotation. Its derivative at a_i gives a 'standard' round disk σ(D_i) in T_{X,a_i}. Equivalently it gives a hermitian norm on the tangent line, recording the conformal radius.

The conjecture finished on this page: the map (D_i) ↦ (σ(D_i)), from admissible systems of conformal disks around the a_i to systems of standard disks in the T_{X,a_i}, is a bijection. The target is a torsor under (R*+)^I, so the source would be one too.

In families over Teichmüller space T_{g,I}, the space TB_{g,I} of surfaces with such disk systems would then be a principal (R*+)^I-bundle over T_{g,I}. Here TB means 'bordered' or decorated Teichmüller space, i.e. surfaces with boundary obtained by removing the disks.

He then draws a consequence. If the relation hypothesized just before held, the bundle would have canonical sections. A point of TB_{g,I} is a (bordered / X_0-rigidified) surface of type (g,ν). Through σ, a canonical section would give canonical norms, i.e. canonical hermitian metrics, on the tangent lines T_{X,a_i}. On the next page he finds this harmless for g ≥ 1, since X carries a canonical metric. For g = 0 he finds it 'strange', since the compact sphere has no canonical metric.

Purpose: this is part of building Teichmüller/moduli theory by conformal surgery, i.e. gluing standard pieces ('pinces', disks) to bordered surfaces. That programme is the Teichmüller-tower / surgery programme of the Esquisse.
errors: Read literally (any disjoint conformal disks), σ cannot be injective. The conformal radius at a_i, one real parameter per point, does not determine the disk: infinitely many Jordan domains have the same conformal radius. The conjecture only makes sense for a restricted class of 'admissible' disks, e.g. those produced by the surgery with boundary data l_i. That class is defined only heuristically here and on the previous page, which is the real gap.

The worry about g = 0 (next page) is unfounded within the hyperbolic case he restricts to. A sphere with ν ≥ 3 punctures (and likewise g = 1 with ν ≥ 1) carries a canonical complete hyperbolic metric with cusps. Each cusp has a canonical local coordinate up to rotation (q = e^{2πiz} on the horoball {Im z > 1}/(z ↦ z+1)). This yields canonical hermitian norms on each T_{X,a_i}, and so canonical sections, for every hyperbolic type, g = 0 included.

Similarly, for g ≥ 2 the relevant canonical metric is the cusped hyperbolic metric of X minus the punctures, not the metric of the compact X. The compact metric would give tangent norms too, but not the canonical ones adapted to the punctures.

Existence of 'canonical sections' does not follow from bijectivity alone. Any principal R_{>0}^I-bundle over a contractible base is trivial, but canonicity needs an extra construction, presumably the 'relation qui précédait', which is not recorded clearly.

ideas.what: Assigning to a conformal disk around a puncture the standard disk / norm it induces on the tangent line (conformal radius)
ideas.modern_name: conformal radius; hermitian metric on the tangent line at a marked point
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Riemann mapping, Koebe); in the moduli context Wolpert, Takhtajan–Zograf

ideas.what: Conjecture that admissible disk systems around the punctures form a torsor under (R*+)^I via σ, giving a principal (R*+)^I-bundle TB_{g,I} → T_{g,I}
ideas.modern_name: decorated Teichmüller space T̃_{g,s} = T_{g,s} × R_{>0}^s (horocycle decorations); Teichmüller space of surfaces with marked disks / local coordinates up to rotation
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Penner (decorated Teichmüller space, 1987); spaces of surfaces with parametrized disks: Segal, Vafa, Kontsevich (late 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions conformal surgery for building Teichmüller towers only in outline

ideas.what: Canonical sections, i.e. canonical metrics on the tangent lines at the punctures, as a test of the conjecture
ideas.modern_name: hyperbolic cusp metric on the tautological (ψ) line bundles; horocycle of fixed length as canonical decoration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Wolpert (cusp metric on ψ-bundles, 2007); Takhtajan–Zograf; Penner (horocycles)

missed.claim: The page conjectures a principal (R*+)^I-bundle over Teichmüller space T_{g,I}, parametrizing disk systems (one positive real per puncture), and links its canonical sections to canonical metrics on the tangent lines at punctures. This prefigures Penner's decorated Teichmüller space (1987) and the cusp-metric description of the ψ-class line bundles. Grothendieck does not see that the hyperbolic cusp structure resolves his g = 0 worry: horocycles give the canonical section in all hyperbolic cases.
missed.quote: cela donnerait donc structure de fibré principal de groupe structural (R*+)^I : TB_{g,I} sur T_{g,I} (card I = ν)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor, c. 1983-84, of decorated Teichmüller theory, arrived at from conformal surgery rather than hyperbolic geometry. It documents Grothendieck's surgery approach to building the Teichmüller tower, which was never written up.

missed.claim: The bijectivity conjecture for 'admissible' disk systems is left open. The notion of admissible disk is only heuristic, tied to the surgery parameters l_i of the previous page.
missed.quote: l'application (D_i) ↦ (σ(D_i)) des syst. admissibles de disques conformes autour des a_i, vers l'ens. des syst. de disques standard dans les T_{X,a_i}, est bijection
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Making 'admissible' precise, e.g. disks cut out by horocycles or by Strebel/Jenkins–Strebel differentials, would turn the conjecture into a known theorem. It would clarify how his surgery picture matches decorated Teichmüller space and ribbon-graph cell decompositions.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, informal anticipation of a decorated-Teichmüller-type R_{>0}^I bundle and of canonical tangent metrics at punctures. However, it is heuristic, partly mistaken (the g = 0 worry), and the objects were later developed independently (Penner, Wolpert). It is notable mainly as unpublished documentation of the surgery programme.
transcription_corrections: 'des syst. de disques ... des les T_{X,a_i}' should read 'dans les T_{X,a_i}'; the inserted word over the crossed-out 'conformes' is likely 'standard'.
'cela donnerait donc [-une-] [-la-] structure de fibré principal de groupe [-TB_{g,I} → T_{g,I}-] structural (R*+)^I : TB_{g,I} sur T_{g,I}' is the intended reading.
'syst. d'ombres canoniques des T_{X,a_i}' is probably 'syst. de normes canoniques sur les T_{X,a_i}'. This matches 'i.e. des métriques riemanniennes canoniques' on the next page.
'une surface {+parfaite+}' is uncertain. The handwriting suggests 'surface à bord' or 'surface bordée' (consistent with TB = bordered Teichmüller), with an insertion possibly reading 'ponctuée'.
The interlinear insertion reads approximately 'Si l'hypothèse/relation (qui précédait)', replacing struck-through text.
